Chapter 12: Becoming Love in Action.
You know, it’s one thing to talk about love—to admire it from afar or agree with the idea of it. But here’s the real challenge: love isn’t meant to just stay in words or theories. It’s meant to be lived, shaping every part of our lives—what we say, what we do, even what we dream about.
Let me tell you about a young couple who decided to spend their weekends volunteering at a local food bank. At first, honestly, it was uncomfortable. It felt a bit awkward, and sometimes inconvenient. But as they started connecting with the people they served, something shifted in them. Their hearts opened up. They began to notice needs they hadn’t seen before, to really listen, to care in ways they never expected. You see, love actually grows through action—not just through good intentions.
Have you ever caught yourself waiting for the “perfect” moment to help someone? Maybe you want to make a difference, but you worry about doing it wrong. Here’s the thing: love isn’t about getting it perfect. It’s about being present. It’s about showing up, even when you’re not sure what to say or do.
There’s a retired nurse I know who started writing letters to people in her community who were going through tough times. She didn’t have fancy words or magical solutions. What she had was a willingness to reach out. And over time, those simple letters became a real source of comfort and hope for dozens of people.
Becoming love means letting go of fear—fear of failing, fear of being rejected, or just not feeling good enough. It means trusting that even the smallest act matters, and that every effort really does count. Most of us don’t realize how much of a difference we can make, simply by being willing to try.
In the end, living out love in action doesn’t just change the world around us—it transforms us, too.
